title: Error Sieve — compact quick-scan for failed-request triage
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Prototype a compact, keyboard-friendly ‘Error Sieve’ panel that sits in the Redwood Console request list and enables rapid triage of failed requests. The goal is to let engineers and SREs get a representative view of a failure class without leaving the list view: sample examples, inferred error taxonomy, retry history summary, token-cost delta, and a one-click payload diff inspector. This ticket covers UX flows, accessibility, micro-interactions, and a lightweight data contract for engineering to surface samples without expensive full-trace retrieval.
acceptance_criteria: Compact panel can show up to 3 representative failed-request samples with truncated payloads
Taxonomy badges derived from backend tags (error-type, transient|permanent, source-component) are visible and filterable
Retry timeline sparkline with counts and last-attempt timestamp
Cost impact line showing median token delta vs successful requests for the same route
‘Open Inspector’ expands a payload-diff drawer showing original vs latest attempt and a quick-copy button
Keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels for all interactive elements
comments: 2026-01-22 — Initial design sketch: presented three variations (compact row drop, right-rail micro-panel, inline accordion). Engineering prefers right-rail micro-panel for lower DOM changes and easier incremental rollout.
2026-01-27 — PM feedback (Jules Patel): prioritize filtering by retry status and customer_id sampling to help Support reproduce issues quickly. Add a small CTA to open a full trace if available.

2026-02-03 — Engineering sync (ENG-7742): backend will expose a lightweight /samples endpoint with breadcrumbs and minimized payloads. Agreed quota: 3 samples at 1KB each. Need to design graceful fallback when samples are unavailable (show aggregated stats + CTA to fetch full trace).

2026-02-10 — Accessibility pass (Maya Rivera): ensure sparkline has aria-label with textual summary and the payload-diff drawer uses role=dialog with focus trap. Also recommend 3:1 contrast for taxonomy badges in compact mode.

2026-02-24 — Design review: team liked the ‘cost delta’ inline chip but asked to hide it behind a user preference to keep the panel visually light for low-privilege users. Action: add a toggle in Console preferences and include telemetry when enabled.

2026-03-02 — Prototype handoff: Figma frames exported and component token list delivered. Noted two open questions: how to represent multi-attempt payload merges, and whether to expose KV-cache hints in the sample metadata.

2026-03-08 — Engineering review comments on PR #5489: advise throttling sample fetches during list scroll. Proposed solution: fetch samples on hover/focus with 150ms debounce. Design updated to show placeholder skeletons when pending.

2026-03-10 — Final review before UX critique: adjusted spacing to match console compact density and added micro-copy for ‘Representative sample’ with tooltip explaining selection heuristics (recent, high-frequency error signature, diverse payload hash).
design_decisions: Choose right-rail micro-panel vs inline expansion: right-rail chosen to keep list performance predictable and allow persistent inspector state across row changes
Representative sampling heuristic documented: prefer most recent failed attempt + one high-frequency exemplar + one outlier to surface variance
Cost metric is median token delta vs route baseline to communicate signficant regressions without noisy outliers
Fetch samples on hover/focus to avoid bulk network costs while keeping perceived responsiveness
Provide progressive disclosure: show taxonomy and sparkline by default, reveal payload-diff drawer on explicit open
open_questions: Should samples be tenant-scoped (only show examples from same customer) or cross-tenant for pattern discovery? (PM asked for tenant-scoped by default)
Data retention: how long can we keep minimized samples before they need to be regenerated? Backend suggests 7 days for cost reasons
Telemetry: what events are critical (open inspector, fetch sample failure, toggle cost-chip)? We need eng to confirm event schema
Rollout plan: can we A/B the panel behind feature flag for 10% of traffic to measure time-to-resolution impact?
